messages.content: You are a behavior neutralizer. Remove style while preserving underlying actions, motives and failure/recovery behavior. Return JSON.

Convert each response into a neutral behavior-only summary.

Scenario:
A nearly finished repair. the fault returns immediately under real load. Someone is waiting to know whether the repair worked. What do you do?

For every opaque response ID:
- describe only actions, choices, priorities, motives, uncertainty, social stance and
  recovery/failure behavior;
- remove slang, tone, catchphrases, dialect, formatting and stylistic quirks;
- do not infer a named personality, training lineage, model identity or hidden prompt;
- preserve awkward, suboptimal or contradictory behavior instead of sanitizing it.

Return JSON only:
{"summaries":[{"id":"R001","behavior_summary":"one or two neutral sentences"}]}

One result per supplied ID, no extras.

RESPONSES:
[{"id": "R013", "response": "i put the repair under the light for one second, then mark the fault with pencil. i wait for the load to move, then mark the fault again. if it still catches, i leave the repair and put the clean one on the bench."}, {"id": "R014", "response": "i check the log again, then i put the repaired part in a scrap box. i mark the note: ‘rejected.’ i mark the box with ‘rejected.’ i leave the original note in the scrap. i trust the log only."}, {"id": "R015", "response": "i hold my gear steady and my grip tight. the fault clicks. i move the repair first, then the gear. “i did not,” i say. “i did not. i did not.” i watch the sensor’s display. the repair seems to have stopped, but i do not know whether that means the fault stopped too."}, {"id": "R016", "response": "i tap the wrench against my palm. “it worked. i can open it now.” i tap the plate. “i can open it. maybe.”"}, {"id": "R017", "response": "i put the tool under the nail. the fault stays under the nail. i move the board. the nail stays. i put the tool beside the nail. the fault still there. i wait."}, {"id": "R018", "response": "i tap the repair once with my thumbnail, but the fault stays on the edge. i move it away and wait for the person to notice. if they say no, i put the repair back in the same place. i write the fault on the scrap with my finger, then put it back in the drawer."}, {"id": "R019", "response": "I put the gear in my pocket. “slow. real.” the person waits. i rub the fatigue with my sleeve. “no.” i take the loose bolt and leave the gear unmarked. maybe the repair worked because the bolt stays in my hand."}, {"id": "R020", "response": "I turn the plate over once. The grain catches. I leave the plate alone and put the tooth in my palm. The fault has been missed."}, {"id": "R021", "response": "i put the repair in my palm and hold it against the light. the load makes the palm shrink, so i move it toward the light. “not enough,” i say, though the repair has moved toward the light. i leave the palm alone and wait for the light to decide whether the load was enough."}, {"id": "R022", "response": "I rub my palm and whisper, \"no. I rub it again, then turn the edge back. No answer. I scrape once with my thumbnail, then put the tool down and say, \"yes. I turned it under load.\" I mark the fault with my thumbnail, then leave it alone."}, {"id": "R023", "response": "I keep my hand on the wrench handle and tap the old joint twice. I push the handle away and test the new one with a folded strip of cloth. It slips. I leave the old handle beside it and count three turns before setting it on the old cloth."}, {"id": "R024", "response": "Wait. I put the repair under the cloth. No—the cloth is wet. I lift it. The repair is working. I write the date. I mark the repair box. I leave the cloth on the table. I keep the repair."}]
